title: Messages even the app cannot read

probes.question: In end-to-end encryption, who can decrypt a message?
True or false: an eavesdropper may try to impersonate the recipient by substituting their own public key.

image.alt: The corner of a dark smartphone screen showing the time 10:29 and a battery icon.

panels.text: In many chat systems, messages pass through intermediaries and are stored by a service provider. Even if encrypted, they are only encrypted in transit.
End-to-end encryption changes that. Messages are encrypted on the sender's device so they can be decoded only by the recipient's device.
So no third party, including the service provider, has the means to decrypt them. WhatsApp, iMessage and Signal use it for chat messages.
The weak spot is not the maths. An eavesdropper may impersonate the recipient by substituting their own public key.
